facts.statement: The genus Vorona is known from fossils found in the Late Cretaceous Maevarano Formation near the village of Berivotra in Madagascar.
facts.quote: known from outcrops of the Late Cretaceous (Maastrichtian age) Maevarano Formation near the village of Berivotra in Mahajanga Province, Madagascar.

facts.statement: The only known species, Vorona berivotrensis, is represented by scattered hindlimb bones that may belong to a single individual.
facts.quote: The genus contains a single species, Vorona berivotrensis, known from scattered hindlimb remains, possibly from a single individual (UA 8651 and FMNH PA715).

facts.statement: Some researchers suggest that Vorona might be a primitive member of the ornithuromorph group.
facts.quote: Vorona might be a primitive ornithuromorph.

facts.statement: Other studies have classified Vorona as an enantiornithean bird.
facts.quote: Some studies have recovered it as an enantiornithean.

facts.statement: The fossil remains of Vorona display a mix of features found in both primitive and modern birds.
facts.quote: al presentar rasgos de aves primitivas y modernas

facts.statement: Confusion with the dromaeosaurid Rahonavis ostromi led to the incorrect idea that Vorona possessed a sickle-shaped claw on each foot.
facts.quote: Esta confusión ha llevado a la idea errónea de que Vorona tenía una garra en forma de hoz en cada pie, parecida a la de los miembros de Deinonychosauria.

facts.statement: The Maevarano Formation where Vorona fossils were found dates to the Campanian stage, between 70.6 and 83.5 million years ago.
facts.quote: Dicha formación data probablemente del Campaniense, hace entre 70.6 a 83.5 millones de años

facts.statement: The Paleobiology Database lists the parent group of Vorona as Ornithuromorpha.
Fossil occurrences of Vorona are recorded from the Maastrichtian stage, between 72.2 and 66 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Maastrichtian to Maastrichtian (72.2 to 66 million years ago)
